title: Pushforward of modules along a closed immersion is fully faithful
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $i_*:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Z)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $i^*$ be the pushforward and pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], with the adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$. Then for every $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ the counit $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}:i^*i_*\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $i_*$ is fully faithful: for all $\mathcal O_Z$-modules $\mathcal G,\mathcal G'$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal G,\mathcal G')\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal G,i_*\mathcal G')$, $\varphi\mapsto i_*\varphi$, is bijective.

proof.text: For G on Z, the unit at i_*G is epimorphic by the epi clause of closedImmersion_unit_kernel. The right triangle identity makes i_*(counit G) its retraction. An epimorphic split monomorphism is invertible, and its retraction is its inverse. Thus the pushed-forward counit is invertible.

At every z in Z, the natural isomorphisms between the stalks of closed pushforwards at i(z) and the original stalks at z conjugate the stalk map of the pushed-forward counit to the stalk map of the counit. The former is an isomorphism since the pushed-forward counit is. Hence the counit is an isomorphism by the stalk criterion and reflection of isomorphisms by the underlying presheaf functor.
Install the componentwise counit isomorphisms, use Adjunction.fullyFaithfulROfIsIsoCounit, and extract injectivity and surjectivity of pushforward on every hom-set.
